question: What must you check before changing lanes?
options: Your mirrors and blind spot
Only your rear-view mirror
Only the speed limit sign
Your horn and hazard lights
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 says you must check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

question: When changing lanes, how should your move affect vehicles in the next lane?
options: They should slow down slightly for you
You must not force them to slow down or swerve
You only need to clear cars behind you
You have priority if you signal first
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 states you must not cut in or force others to slow down.

question: Why should you look over your shoulder before moving into another lane?
options: To check your rear tyres
Because mirrors do not show every blind spot
To wave thank you to cars behind
To see if your brake lights work
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 warns that mirrors cannot cover every blind spot beside your car.

question: In slow queuing traffic, when should you change lanes?
options: Whenever a tiny gap opens for a moment
Only when it is safe and you will not block others
As fast as possible before the queue stops
Without signalling so others do not speed up
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 advises not weaving between lanes or cutting across other drivers.

question: What should you do right after checking your mirrors before changing lanes?
options: Check your blind spot over your shoulder
Speed up sharply
Flash your brake lights
Turn on hazard lights
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 says to check mirrors and blind spots before changing lanes.

question: Before moving back to the left lane after overtaking, what must you be sure of?
options: There is plenty of room ahead of the passed vehicle
The car behind flashes its lights
You are going at least 70 mph
Your left indicator is off
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 warns not to cut in front of the vehicle you overtook.

question: When a lane ahead is closed by cones, when should you merge?
options: Early and smoothly when you see a safe gap
At the very last cone by forcing in
By driving onto the pavement
Without using any signal
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 advises changing lanes smoothly in good time.

question: What can happen if you change lanes without checking your blind spot?
options: You could hit a cyclist, rider, or car beside you
Your tyres wear out faster
Your fuel gauge drops
Your horn stops working
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 highlights that motorcycles and cars can hide in blind spots.

question: If the lane you want to enter has faster traffic, what should you do?
options: Pull out and let them brake
Wait for a safe gap so they do not have to slow down
Signal for one second then steer
Straddle the white line
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 requires waiting so faster vehicles do not have to slow down.

question: On a three-lane road, why should you avoid changing two lanes in one sweep?
options: It wastes fuel
You cannot check all blind spots and traffic at once
It is only allowed for lorries
Road paint becomes slippery
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 says to make each lane change carefully with fresh checks.

question: When two lanes merge into one, how should you treat a driver alongside you?
options: Race ahead to beat them
Leave space and merge in turn safely
Block them with your car
Sound your horn continuously
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 and merging advice promote safe, courteous lane changes.

question: In heavy rain, why do blind-spot checks matter even more before changing lanes?
options: Spray reduces what you can see in side mirrors
Wipers turn off automatically
Indicators flash slower
Speed limits double
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 and wet-weather advice warn that spray hides vehicles in mirrors.

question: You see a motorcycle filtering between lanes as you plan to move right. What should you do?
options: Steer right anyway because you are bigger
Hold your lane and wait until the rider has passed safely
Open your door to warn them
Brake hard in your lane
explain: Highway Code Rule 133 requires watching for motorcyclists before changing lanes.
